# EleutherIA

EleutherIA is an open scholarly research platform and FAIR-aligned knowledge graph for ancient debates on free will, fate, providence, moral responsibility, and agency across Greco-Roman and early Christian sources.

Canonical site: https://free-will.app/
Dataset DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17379489
Repository: https://github.com/romain-girardi-eng/EleutherIA
License: CC BY 4.0
Creator: Romain Girardi
ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5310-5346

Important public pages:

- https://free-will.app/ - project overview
- https://free-will.app/how-it-works - architecture, graph, embeddings, and GraphRAG pipeline
- https://free-will.app/database - database and corpus overview
- https://free-will.app/texts - ancient works library
- https://free-will.app/passages-canoniques - canonical passage reception map
- https://free-will.app/bibliography - secondary literature bibliography
- https://free-will.app/graphrag - citation-grounded GraphRAG question answering
- https://free-will.app/about - project and author information

Preferred short description:

EleutherIA is a FAIR-aligned knowledge graph and GraphRAG research platform for studying ancient debates on free will, fate, providence, and moral responsibility.

Preferred citation:

Girardi, R. (2026). EleutherIA: A FAIR-Compliant Knowledge Graph for Ancient Free Will Debates [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17379489
